questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good university with interesting topics regarding my education, English-speaking country, a good city with nice surroundings.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing exchange stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was mostly easy with the orientation sessions, but it was at times difficult to navigate in informations and steps needed from both my home and host universities.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not applicable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I didn't search much for it, but most of the welcome gatherings / get to meet other students things were cancelled due to Covid, so there wasn't many opportunities.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I ended up in a studio apartment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Options were available, but I chose not to participate.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Campus is a bit disconnected from the city of Vancouver, and it is quite expensive. It does give you that "campus feel" though which I enjoyed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's been a while, but I had to apply for the exchange stay, accept my spot and then fill in many documents. It wasn't always easy to have an overview of deadlines etc., but fortunately help was there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got help from friends, the recorded orientation sessions and being in contact with the person managing exchange stays in North America.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted, there was one class I didn't get into, but I only needed three courses so it was all good.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep track of what needs to be done, it can be a bit overwhelming at times.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was good. I only had third year classes, corresponding pretty well to my current state of education.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More focus on teaching from the professors I believe, but not as much group work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GEOG 310: Environment and sustainability
GEOG 314: Analyzing environmental problems
GEOS 307: Biogeography and global change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: GEOS 307: Biogeography and global change was a very interesting course on a geographical topic not much elaborated in UCPH.
